newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-SWEDISH STRIKER COULD MAKE HIS PEACE WITH LEEDS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SWEDISH STRIKER COULD MAKE HIS PEACE WITH LEEDS.

text.p: Swedish international Tomas Brolin said on Friday he could still have a future at Leeds United and wants fresh talks with manager George Graham.
Brolin's last meeting with his new boss broke up with the club claiming the player did not want to return to the English premier league club, but now the Swede insists he never said this.
"I never closed the door on Leeds," he told the Yorkshire Evening Post newspaper.

"You never know, the wind can change direction. I never said I wouldn't play for Leeds again. What I did say was that it would be hard for me to come back at the moment because I am not fit enough to do myself or the club justice.
"I need to play football and I need to speak to Leeds again to see if we can find a solution to this situation."
Brolin was signed by former Leeds boss Howard Wilkinson for 4.5 million pounds ($7 million) 11 months ago, but struggled with injury and lack of form towards the end of last season.
In the close season, Brolin joined FC Zurich on loan and claims he had a gentleman's agreement with Wilkinson to stay there until December in order to regain his match fitness.
But now Leeds are demanding, as he is under contract with them, that he either plays for them or faces an 18-month period out of the professional game.
"I really needed to play more games in Zurich," added Brolin. "I have a problem with my stomach muscles and this is something I would have improved by staying and playing in Zurich.
"If I had come back to Leeds now, I would not have been fit enough and the last thing I wanted to do was let down the Leeds fans who have been so good to me.
"It is very boring not being able to play football. That's what I do to live and I really need to be playing somewhere.
"But Leeds have gone back on a gentleman's agreement and now I am not playing at all. I have missed three or four matches with Zurich now when I really want to be playing."
